Unfortunately, it sounds like you're dealing with probably the worst situation with passive aggression: done in private/sparsely populated locations. That makes it difficult to garnish attention upon the passive insults and display the person as an aggressor in the eyes of others, and the lack of witnesses can turn any confrontation into a matter of hearsay and lies/exaggerations.

As unhelpful as this sounds, the best solution is to not care. At the end of it all, if you look at your interactions with her through the lens of "How much am I going to care/remember about these instances in 5 years", it can make the effort she put into annoying you look comically small. She wants to wrap herself around your ex's dick, what does it matter to you? He's an ex for I'm sure a number of reasons, and unless you're still emotionally attached to him, how much will their actions effect you both short and long terms? Headphones, long term perspective, and understanding that cunts do what they do because they are cunts - all of that can make her attempts to be mean appear more humorous instead.

Beyond that, try to spend more time working out with a gym buddy or group. That brings people that can be witnesses to the snide comments, and that exposure can be weaponized to paint the passive aggressor as the offensive party. The point of being passive aggressive is to insult someone in a manner that gives them reasonable deniability if you counteract their actions with any overt aggression or insults. If you can get them to lose the veil of deniability, it opens up more direct options and makes any response you take have a better light in the eyes of others because it's more of a retaliatory response instead of the primary aggressor.

I usually divide my options into two categories based on a question: How much power and influence they can have on my life? With people of authority, at work, customers, etc. I take a more delicate approach than to someone who has no way of effecting me outside of an emotional response. For the former of the two, I bait them into open aggression; for the latter I engage openly. As a side note I'm generally a blunt and confrontational person; due to experience, I find the idea of "not stooping to their level" to be a weak attempt at avoiding conflict that leaves you on the receiving end of continuous abuse. I find "I'll get down to your level and drown you in your own mud" to be a more effective ideal at ending perpetual annoyances.

If I'm going to openly engage, it's generally a "It sounds like you're calling me an asshole" or something along the lines of bringing the underlying insult to the surface. It can make them have to leave their comfort zone and be open about what they are saying. If they confirm that, I bluntly ask them why they didn't just come out and say that. "Were you worried about X Y or Z if you just came out and said that instead of trying to hide it?" It can paint them in a number of negative ways. If they deny trying to be insulting, it's a simple matter of asking what they meant by their comment, and when they reply with a more positive sounding answer, quickly responding with something like "I don't know, the way you said [comment] doesn't really sound like what you just claimed it did. It sounded more like [veiled insult]" to really to reveal the insult for those around you. If the surrounding people can see the underhanded comment for what it is, it opens up the options to respond without letting the passive aggressor be able to claim the victim. It also allows for condescending remarks when they try to be passive aggressive again. "We've been through this. Don't be a coward and hide behind veiled comments. You're an adult, say what you mean." Once it opens up, it also lets me use harsh insults as a retort. I always try to keep something that hits at a really personal level in my back pocket to bring out and dwarf anything they can say - "You know, thank god you had a miscarriage. You're such a cunt that I really pity any kids you might have, cause you're going to seriously fuck them up". That one lost me some points with friends, but that ended any further attempts at making verbal jabs at me.

If I'm in a situation where what I say can effect me in a place like a job, I stick with trying to bait the person into being openly aggressive. Usually I coyly and inquisitively ask them to repeat what they said a bit louder "because I didn't quite hear all of that". If they don't, I just retort "Because it sounded like you said [veiled insult]"; if they do, I just move on to asking something akin to "What did you mean by that?". I try to keep them out of their comfort zone and force them to openly iterate the insulting message they are trying to convey; it allows me to flip the role and let's me play the victim while keeping the attention on them. It makes them have to operate and engage in a manner they aren't used to, and that can cause them to mess up their usual act. Depending where the interaction goes, I try and keep pushing it so that it looks like I'm being unfairly insulted, or ask why they didn't just say the openly aggressive insults first instead of hiding behind a little act. The end game for this is to either make the other person look like a complete ass to the others around, both in the actual insult and in the way they tried to hide it.
